name: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church
reason: Memorial instituted 2018 (Monday after Pentecost); searches for 'mater ecclesiae' / 'matris ecclesiae' return nothing in any of the three tracked missals. The 2018 collect is a fresh composition with no pre-1931 printed antecedent.

name: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
reason: The 1862 Pustet has a full proper Mass 'Feria VI post Octav. Ss. Corp. Christi — In Festo Ss. Cordis Jesu' at line 63736, with introit Miserebitur and collect 'Concede, quaesumus omnipotens Deus: ut qui in sanctissimo dilecti Filii tui Corde gloriantes, praecipua in nos caritatis ejus beneficia recolimus...'; leaf n538 (p. 453) was fetched and shows the Mass's closing postcommunio 'Pacificis pasti deliciis... qui mitis es et humilis corde'. The 2002 collect keeps this opening but replaces the final clause, so the source covers most but not all of the current text.

name: Mary, the Holy Mother of God
reason: The current 1 January collect 'Deus, qui salutis aeternae, beatae Mariae virginitate fecunda, humano generi praemia praestitisti...' is verbatim the collect of the Circumcision / Octave of the Nativity: 1862 line 16597 (also 17621), 1604 line 13538, 1570 lines 11229/11733/11919 and calendar line 463. Leaf n124 (p. 39) was fetched and shows the whole collect cleanly printed as 'De S. Maria. Oratio.'

name: Our Lady of Fatima
reason: Apparitions of 1917, Mass approved 1930s and inserted in the general calendar in 2002; 'fatima' returns zero hits in all three missals. No pre-1931 printed Missal can contain it.

name: Our Lady of Loreto
reason: The 1862 Pustet 'pro aliquibus locis' appendix has 'Die x. In Festo Translationis Almae Domus B. M. V.' at line 92642. Leaf n782 (p. [113]) was fetched and shows introit 'Terribilis est locus iste' and the full collect 'Deus, qui beatae Mariae Virginis domum per incarnati Verbi mysterium misericorditer consecrasti, eamque in sinu Ecclesiae tuae mirabiliter collocasti: concede; ut segregati a tabernaculis peccatorum, digni efficiamur habitatores domus sanctae tuae.' — the historic Loreto collect, in clean legible type.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
reason: Searches for 'guadalup' and 'mexic' return zero hits in all three missals; the feast was a Mexican/American indult proper and is absent from the Roman books tracked here. No publishable Latin in this repository's terms.

name: The Most Holy Name of Jesus
reason: The 1862 Pustet has a full proper 'Dominica II post Epiphaniam — In Festo SS. Nominis Jesu' at line 54881: introit 'In nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur' and collect 'Deus, qui Unigenitum Filium tuum constituisti humani generis Salvatorem...', which is the text of the current 3 January optional memorial's collect. Absent from 1604 and 1570 (the feast was only extended to the universal calendar in 1721).

name: The Epiphany of the Lord
reason: Present in all three: 1862 line 16918 'IN EPIPHANIA DOMINI', 1604 line 13638, 1570 line 10702 (calendar line 468). The collect 'Deus, qui hodierna die Unigenitum tuum gentibus stella duce revelasti' is retained unchanged in the postconciliar Missal, so the Latin is fully attested pre-1931.

name: The Nativity of the Lord
reason: Present in all three with the three Masses (night/dawn/day): 1862 line 14901 'IN NATIVITATE DOMINI' (further Masses at 15239, 15430), 1604 line 10932, 1570 line 7986. The Christmas orations are ancient (Veronense/Gelasianum/Hadrianum) and carry over into the postconciliar Missal.

name: Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, Bishops and Doctors of the Church
reason: Both saints are present but only separately and on other dates: 1862 has 'S. Basilii, Episc. Conf. et Doctoris' (14 June) at line 64613 with collect 'Exaudi, quaesumus Domine, preces nostras, quas in beati Basilii...' and 'S. Gregorii Nazianzeni' (9 May) at line 62749 referred to the Common of Doctors; 1604 has both at lines 47117 and 3438. There is no joint 2 January Mass in any pre-1931 Missal (that day was the Octave of St Stephen), and the current joint collect appears to be a 1970 composition, so a PD source exists for the saints but not demonstrably for the postconciliar oration.

name: Saint Raymond of Penyafort, Priest
reason: 1862 Pustet line 56455, 'S. Raymundi de Pennafort, Confessoris' (23 January in the old calendar), Mass Os justi from the Common with proper collect 'Deus, qui beatum Raymundum poenitentiae sacramenti insignem ministrum elegisti, et per maris undas mirabiliter traduxisti...' — the same collect carried into the current 7 January memorial. Absent from 1604 and 1570 (canonised 1601).

name: Saint Hilary, Bishop and Doctor of the Church
reason: Present in all three at 14 January: 1862 line 55143 'S. Hilarii Episcopi, Conf. et Eccl. Doctoris' with proper collect 'Deus, qui populo tuo aeternae salutis beatum Hilarium ministrum tribuisti...', 1604 line 41746 (calendar 2558), 1570 calendar line 476. The current collect is a revision of this ancient text, so the PD witness covers the substance; a text-level collation is still advisable.

name: Saint Anthony, Abbot
reason: Present in all three at 17 January: 1862 line 55584 with full proper (introit 'Os justi meditabitur sapientiam', collect 'Intercessio nos, quaesumus Domine, beati Antonii Abbatis commendet: ut, quod nostris meritis non valemus, ejus patrocinio assequamur'), 1604 lines 41919/42874, 1570 calendar line 481 and 'In festo Antonij Abbatis' at line 57530. The collect is unchanged in the postconciliar Missal.

name: Saint Fabian, Pope and Martyr; Saint Sebastian, Martyr
reason: Joint feast at 20 January in all three: 1862 line 56163 'Ss. Fabiani et Sebastiani, Martyrum' (fol. 388) with proper introit 'Intret in conspectu tuo Domine', 1604 lines 42213/43173 ('sanctis martyribus tuis Fabiano et Sebastiano'), 1570 calendar line 486. Leaf n784 (p. [115]) was fetched and cross-references 'Die xx. Ss. Fabiani et Sebastiani, Martyrum. Missa ut in Missali. fol. 388', confirming the page-image route. The postconciliar calendar splits them into two optional memorials, so the two collects would need to be drawn separately.

name: Saint Blaise, Bishop and Martyr; Saint Ansgar, Bishop
reason: Blaise stands at 3 Feb in the 1862 Pustet (line 58011, indexed to printed p. 404 at line 107625) and in the 1604 typica (index line 62397, feast on printed p. 377 at line 44241); both assign the public-domain Mass 'Sacerdotes Dei' from the Common of one Martyr Bishop rather than a proper collect. Ansgar is absent from all three witnesses (no hit for Ansgar/Anschar).

name: Saint Jerome Emiliani; Saint Josephine Bakhita, Virgin
reason: The 1862 Pustet has a full proper for S. Hieronymi Aemiliani at its pre-1969 date of 20 July (line 68552, printed p. 493), including the collect 'Deus misericordiarum Pater ... quem orphanis adiutorem et patrem esse voluisti', which is the ancestor of the 2002 collect now kept on 8 Feb. Josephine Bakhita (canonised 2000) is absent from all three, as expected.

name: Saint Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor of the Church
reason: No hit for 'Narek' in any of the three tracked missals. Gregory of Narek was added to the General Roman Calendar only in 2021, so no pre-1931 printed Missal can contain his formulary.

name: Saint George, Martyr; Saint Adalbert, Bishop and Martyr
reason: George has a proper Mass in all three: 1862 line 60889 with the collect 'Deus, qui nos beati Georgii Martyris tui meritis et intercessione laetificas' (verbatim the 2002 collect), 1604 line 45266, 1570 lines 712 (calendar) and 60785 (same collect). Adalbert is in the 1862 'Missae pro aliquibus locis' appendix, line 102841, with a proper collect ('Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui hodierna die beatum Adalbertum...'), at appendix printed p. x, about leaf 869; the appendix pagination was checked on leaf 871 (= p. xii).

name: Saint Peter Chanel, Priest and Martyr; Saint Louis Grignion de Montfort, Priest
reason: No hit for 'Chanel' or 'Montfort' in any tracked missal. Peter Chanel was canonised in 1954 and Louis-Marie Grignion de Montfort in 1947, both after every pre-1931 witness the repository holds. In the 1862 the 28 April slot is S. Vitalis (confirmed on leaf 516, printed p. 431).

name: Saint John of Avila, Priest and Doctor of the Church
reason: Absent from all three. John of Avila was canonised in 1970 and made a Doctor in 2012; no pre-1931 Missal can carry his formulary.

name: Saints Nereus and Achilleus, Martyrs; Saint Pancras, Martyr
reason: All three carry the joint Mass of Nereus, Achilleus, Domitilla and Pancras on 12 May: 1862 line 62856 (printed p. 444) with the collect 'Semper nos, Domine, Martyrum tuorum Nerei, Achillei, Domitillae atque Pancratii foveat ... beata sollemnitas', which is the 2002 collect minus Domitilla and Pancras; 1604 lines 46395-46480; 1570 lines 760 and 62181-62239. Pancras has no separate proper collect there, only his place in the joint formulary.

name: Saints Christopher Magallanes, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
reason: No hit for 'Magallan'. The Mexican martyrs died 1926-1928 and were canonised in 2000; no pre-1931 Missal contains them.

name: Saint Rita of Cascia, Religious
reason: No hit for 'Ritae' or 'Cassia' in any tracked missal, and the 1862 sanctorale skips from 20 May (line 63233) straight to 25 May (line 63326), leaving 22 May empty. Rita was canonised in 1900, after the 1862 Pustet; a pre-1931 source could exist in the 1920 typica but that edition is tracked without full text.

name: Saint Bede the Venerable, Priest and Doctor of the Church; Saint Gregory VII, Pope; Saint Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi, Virgin
reason: Two of the three saints are in the 1862 Pustet with proper collects: Gregory VII at 25 May (line 63328, 'Deus in te sperantium fortitudo ... virtute constantiae roborasti', identical to the 2002 collect) and Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi at 27 May (line 63648, 'Deus, virginitatis amator ... puritate et caritate imitemur', also the 2002 collect); leaf 536 was fetched and shows printed p. 451 with the de' Pazzi formulary in full. Bede himself is absent (his feast entered the universal calendar only in 1899); the only 'Bedae' hits are OCR noise from 'Zebedaei'.

name: Saint Paul VI, Pope
reason: Absent by necessity: Paul VI died in 1978 and was canonised in 2018. In the 1862 the 29 May slot is unoccupied; 30 May is S. Felicis (line 63707).

name: Saint Paulinus of Nola, Bishop; Saints John Fisher, Bishop, and Thomas More, Martyrs
reason: Paulinus of Nola is at 22 June in all three: 1862 line 65342 (printed p. 465) with the collect 'Da quaesumus omnipotens Deus, ut beati Paulini Confessoris tui atque Pontificis veneranda sollemnitas', 1604 lines 47506-47533, 1570 lines 854 and 63263. Note the 2002 collect for Paulinus is a fresh composition, so the public-domain text is a witness to the feast rather than to that exact oration. Fisher and More were canonised in 1935 and are absent from all three.

name: Saints Augustine Zhao Rong, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
reason: No hit for 'Zhao'. The Chinese martyrs were canonised as a group in 2000; no pre-1931 Missal contains them.

name: Saint Apollinaris, Bishop and Martyr
reason: Apollinaris has a full proper at his pre-1969 date of 23 July: 1862 line 68967, and leaf 582 was fetched and read, showing printed p. 497 with the secret 'Respice, Domine, propitius super haec munera, quae pro beati Sacerdotis et Martyris tui Apollinaris commemoratione deferimus' and the postcommunion 'Tua sancta sumentes ... beati Apollinaris nos foveant continuata praesidia'. Also 1604 line 49255 and the 1570 calendar at line 948 ('23 Apollinaris episcopi et martyris, semiduplex').

name: Saint Sharbel Makhluf, Priest
reason: Zero hits for Charbel/Sharbel/Makhluf in all three tracked Missals (1570, 1604, 1862). He died 1898 and was canonised 1977, so no pre-1931 printed Missal can contain his Mass; the 2002 proper is a modern composition.

name: Saint Eusebius of Vercelli, Bishop; Saint Peter Julian Eymard, Priest
reason: Eusebius of Vercelli is in the 1862 sanctorale at 16 December (line 54673, calendar entry line 7104) and indexed in the 1604 (line 5413, 'Eusebij Vercellensis Episcopi & mart. commem.'), but in both he is a commemoration whose Mass is taken wholly from the Common ('Missa. Sacerdotes Dei ... ut in Communi unius Martyris Pontificis') with no proper oration printed, so the tracked Missals supply no proper Latin collect for him. Peter Julian Eymard (d. 1868, canonised 1962) is absent from all three.

name: Saints Sixtus II, Pope, and Companions, Martyrs; Saint Cajetan, Priest
reason: The 1862 prints a proper collect for Xystus, Felicissimus and Agapitus at line 70568 ('Deus, qui nos concedis sanctorum Martyrum tuorum Xysti, Felicissimi et Agapiti natalitia colere: da nobis in aeterna beatitudine de eorum societate gaudere'), which is word-for-word the collect still used on 7 August, plus proper secret and postcommunion (lines 70682, 70708) and a Mass 'Ss. Martyrum Xysti et Sociorum' at line 70722; the 1604 also carries these martyrs (index line 4376, orations at lines 50237/50327). Cajetan has a full proper Mass with collect at line 70735 ('Deus, qui beato Cajetano Confessori tuo Apostolicam vivendi formam imitari tribuisti...'), matching the current collect apart from 'Confessori tuo' being modernised to 'presbytero'.

name: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross, Virgin and Martyr
reason: No hits for 'Edith' or 'Benedicta a Cruce' in any of the three Missals. Edith Stein died in 1942 and was canonised in 1998; no pre-1931 Missal can contain her, and the 2002 proper is a modern composition.

name: Saint Maximilian Mary Kolbe, Priest and Martyr
reason: The only 'Maximiliani' hits in the 1862 (lines 105069, 108321) are St Maximilian, Bishop and Martyr, 12 October in the appendix - a different saint, confirmed on the page image at leaf 888 ('Die xii. S. Maximiliani, Episc. et Martyris. Missa. Sacerdotes Dei. de Communi'). Kolbe died 1941 and was canonised 1982; no PD Latin source.

name: Saint Louis; Saint Joseph Calasanz, Priest
reason: Louis IX has a full proper Mass in the 1862 at 25 August: collect at line 72606 ('Deus, qui beatum Ludovicum Confessorem tuum, de terreno regno ad coelestis regni gloriam transtulisti...'), secret at 72721, postcommunion at 72738; the 1604 carries the same feast (index line 4431, orations at lines 51243 and 51286). The current collect is a demonstrable revision of this text, keeping the 'Deus, qui beatum Ludovicum ... transtulisti' frame. Joseph Calasanz also has a proper Mass in the 1862 at 27 August with collect at line 72771ff ('Deus, qui per sanctum Josephum Confessorem tuum, ad erudiendam spiritu intelligentiae ac pietatis juventutem...'), though the 1969 revision of his collect departs further from it.

name: Saint Teresa of Calcutta, Virgin
reason: Zero hits for 'Calcutt' in any of the three Missals. She died 1997 and was canonised 2016; the Mass was added to the General Roman Calendar in 2016, so no PD Latin source can exist.

name: Saint Peter Claver, Priest
reason: The 1862 Appendix Missarum carries a full proper Mass 'B. Petri Claver, Conf. Societatis Jesu' at 9 September (line 104796); page image leaf n885 read and confirmed legible, printed page xxvi, with introit Confiteantur Domino (Ps. 106) and collect 'Deus, qui miserabilia mancipia ad agnitionem tui nominis vocaturus, beatum Petrum Confessorem tuum mira in eis juvandis sui abnegatione et eximia caritate roborasti...'. Caveat: this is the pre-canonisation Jesuit proper (he was beatified 1851, canonised 1888), and I could not verify against the 2002 Missal's collect, which appears to be a later recasting; what is certainly publishable is this 1862 proper itself.

name: The Most Holy Name of Mary
reason: Strongest case in this batch. The 1862 has the full proper Mass 'Festum Ss. Nominis B. Mariae Virg.' (line 73665ff); page image leaf n621 read and confirmed, printed page 536, giving the collect verbatim as the 2002 Missal still has it: 'Concede, quaesumus omnipotens Deus: ut fideles tui, qui sub sanctissimae virginis Mariae Nomine, et protectione laetantur; ejus pia intercessione, a cunctis malis liberentur in terris, et ad gaudia aeterna pervenire mereantur in coelis.' The page also carries the proper secret, communion and postcommunion. Absent from 1570 and 1604 as expected (feast instituted 1683).

name: Saint Robert Bellarmine, Bishop and Doctor of the Church; Saint Hildegard of Bingen, Virgin and Doctor of the Church
reason: Zero hits for 'Bellarmin' or 'Hildegard' in all three Missals. Bellarmine was canonised in 1930 and his feast inserted in 1932, after the 1931 cut-off and after all three tracked editions; Hildegard was never in the Roman Missal before her 2012 equipollent canonisation and doctorate.

name: Saints Andrew Kim Tae-gon, Priest, Paul Chong Ha-sang, and Companions, Martyrs
reason: No hits for Kim, Ha-sang or Coreae in any of the three Missals (the single 1604 hit for 'coreas' at line 23793 is OCR noise inside a scripture pericope). The Korean martyrs were canonised in 1984; no PD Latin source.

name: Saint Pius of Pietrelcina, Priest
reason: No hits for Pietrelcina or Forgione in any of the three Missals (the 1570 hit at line 193 is 'Scipio de Octavianis', a printer's colophon). Padre Pio died 1968 and was canonised 2002; no PD Latin source.

name: Saint Wenceslaus, Martyr; Saints Lawrence Ruiz and Companions, Martyrs
reason: The 1862 has St Wenceslaus at 28 September (calendar line 6163, Mass at line 75348) with a proper collect: 'Deus, qui beatum Wenceslaum per Martyrii palmam a terreno principatu ad coelestem gloriam transtulisti: ejus precibus nos ab omni adversitate custodi, et ejusdem tribue gaudere consortio' - the same text the current Missal keeps, with 'beatum Wenceslaum' expanded to 'beatum martyrem Wenceslaum'. Absent from 1570 and 1604 as expected (feast extended to the universal calendar in 1670). Lawrence Ruiz and companions (canonised 1987) are absent from all three and have no PD source.

name: Saint Faustina Kowalska, Virgin
reason: All 1862 'Faustin' hits are Ss. Faustinus and Jovita (15 February, lines 58529, 93661) and Faustinus among the companions of Pope Felix - different saints. Faustina Kowalska died 1938 and was canonised 2000; the Mass entered the General Roman Calendar in 2020. No PD Latin source.

name: Saints Denis, Bishop, and Companions, Martyrs; Saint John Leonardi, Priest; Saint John Henry Newman, Priest and Doctor of the Church
reason: Ss. Dionysii, Rustici et Eleutherii have a full proper at 1862 line 76208, confirmed on leaf 642 (p. 557, 'Festa Octobris. (9.)') with the collect 'Deus, qui hodierna die beatum Dionysium Martyrem tuum atque Pontificem virtute constantiae in passione roborasti'; the same feast is at 1570 line 70591 and 1604 line 52798. John Leonardi additionally has a full proper Mass (introit, collect, epistle) in the Pustet 'pro aliquibus locis' appendix at line 105890, confirmed on leaf 895 (fol. XXXIVb, 'Die ix. Octobris, In Festo B. Joannis Leonardi'). John Henry Newman (d. 1890, canonized 2019) is absent from all three and cannot appear in any pre-1931 Missal.

name: Saint John XXIII, Pope
reason: Angelo Roncalli died in 1963 and was canonized in 2014; searches for 'Ioannis XXIII' and 'Roncalli' return nothing in any of the three tracked Missals. No pre-1931 printed Missal can contain this feast, so no publishable Latin source exists in this repository's terms.

name: Saint Hedwig, Religious; Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque, Virgin
reason: S. Hedwigis, Reginae Viduae stands at 1862 line 76620, confirmed on leaf 645 (p. 560) with the proper collect 'Deus, qui beatam Hedwigem a saeculi pompa ad humilem tuae crucis sequelam toto corde transire docuisti'. Margaret Mary Alacoque has a complete proper (Oratio, Secreta, Postcommunio) in the Pustet appendix at line 106738, confirmed on leaf 903, 'Die xvii. Octobris, In Festo B. Margaritae Mariae Alacoque, Virginis', collect 'Domine Jesu Christe, qui investigabiles divitias cordis tui beatae Margaritae Virgini mirabiliter revelasti' — the same composition the postconciliar missal retains. The appendix carries its own imprimatur (Ratisbonae 31. Mart. 1865), well before 1931. Neither saint appears in the 1604 or 1570.

name: Saints John de Brébeuf and Isaac Jogues, Priests, and Companions, Martyrs; Saint Paul of the Cross, Priest
reason: Only the Paul of the Cross half is covered. 'B. Pauli a Cruce, Confessoris' has a full proper in the Pustet 'pro aliquibus locis' appendix at line 101105, confirmed on leaf 853 (fol. [184], 'Festa Novembris (14. 15. 16.) pro aliqu. locis' — he was then kept on 16 November), collect 'Domine Jesu Christe, qui ad recolenda Passionis tuae mysteria, ejusque memoriam excitandam, beatum Paulum elegisti'. Brébeuf and Jogues were canonized in 1930 and searches for 'Brebeuf', 'Iogues' and 'Canadens' return nothing in any of the three Missals; that half has no public-domain source here.

name: Saint John Paul II, Pope
reason: Karol Wojtyła died in 2005 and was canonized in 2014; searches for 'Wojtyla' and 'Ioannis Pauli' return nothing in any tracked Missal. A twentieth-century saint cannot be in a pre-1931 Missal, so no publishable Latin source exists.

name: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed (All Souls)
reason: 'MISSAE PRO DEFUNCTIS — In Commemoratione Omnium Fidelium Defunctorum' opens at 1862 line 89927, confirmed on leaf 759 (a colour-printed page) carrying the introit Requiem aeternam and the collect 'Fidelium Deus omnium Conditor et Redemptor, animabus famulorum famularumque tuarum, remissionem cunctorum tribue peccatorum' — the very oration the postconciliar missal keeps as the first All Souls collect. The Missa Defunctorum is likewise in the 1570 (line 2155 ff.) and the 1604. This is the strongest case in the batch.

name: Saint Margaret of Scotland; Saint Gertrude, Virgin
reason: Both saints have propers in the 1862. 'S. Margaritae, Reginae Scotiae' at line 64216, confirmed on leaf 541 (p. 456, 'Die x' of June, her pre-1969 date), collect 'Deus, qui beatam Margaritam Reginam eximia in pauperes caritate mirabilem effecisti'. 'S. Gertrudis, Virginis' at line 78575, confirmed on leaf 662 (p. 577, 'Die xv' of November), collect 'Deus, qui in corde beatae Gertrudis Virginis jucundam tibi mansionem praeparasti'. Both read as the compositions the postconciliar missal carries forward. Neither is in the 1604 or 1570.

name: Saint Clement I, Pope and Martyr; Saint Columban, Abbot
reason: 'S. Clementis, Papae et Martyris' at 1862 line 79114 with the collect 'Deus, qui nos annua beati Clementis Martyris tui atque Pontificis solemnitate laetificas'; leaf 668 (p. 583, 'Festa Novembris. (23. 24.)') was fetched and shows the tail of his Mass, so the Mass opens on leaf 667. Also 1570 line 72273 ('In festo Sancti Clementis'). Columban is absent from all three — he entered the general calendar only in 1969, and 'Columbani' returns no hit in any edition — so that half has no public-domain source.

name: Saints Andrew Dung-Lac, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
reason: The Vietnamese martyrs were canonized in 1988. Searches for 'Dung', 'Tunkin', 'Tonkin', 'Annamit' and 'Vietnam' produce no genuine hit in any tracked Missal (the single 1570 match, line 29211, is OCR noise in an unrelated passage). No publishable Latin source exists here.

name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Virgin and Martyr
reason: 'S. Catharinae, Virg. et Martyris' at 1862 line 79462, confirmed on leaf 669 (p. 584, 'Die xxv'), Mass Loquebar from the Common with the proper collect 'Deus, qui dedisti legem Moysi in summitate montis Sinai, et in eodem loco, per sanctos Angelos tuos, corpus beatae Catharinae Virginis et Martyris tuae mirabiliter collocasti'. Present in all three: 1604 line 62404 ('Catharinae virginis et martyris, xxv. Novembris') and 1570 line 72424.

name: Saint Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin
reason: Juan Diego was canonized in 2002 and his memorial is a modern addition; 'Guadalup' returns nothing in any edition. The nine 'Didaci' hits in the 1862 are S. Didacus of Alcalá (13 November, leaf 662 p. 577), an unrelated saint. No pre-1931 Missal can supply this Latin.
